160: The driver is `run-subset.sh`, a copy of `explorations/compile-ladder/run-ladder.sh` restricted by `subset.txt` and given a ladder root and output directory inside this worktree, so its cache pruning cannot touch a parallel run. The inherited copy could not run at all -- it sourced `env.sh` one directory level too high -- which is why the first launch's last log is two lines of `unbound variable`; the path is fixed and matches rung 3's copy of the same driver (`rung3/run-subset.sh:11`).
161: 
162: The subset is every program in `ProjectFortress/tests/` that declares a variable at the top level of a component: I re-derived it with a column-anchored grep and it is exactly the inherited twenty -- nineteen matched by `^var` or `^name: T :=`, plus `XXXmutableTopVarWithoutType.fss`, whose `var (x, y) = (1, 2)` my expression missed and which `forVarDeclPrePass` rejects as a tupled left-hand side either way.
163: 
164: The "before" is the ladder re-run of the whole climb, `explorations/compile-ladder/after/results.tsv` (commit `266e437a`), which is a legitimate baseline for this rung: `git diff 266e437a 49ee5e91 -- ProjectFortress/src ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin Library build.xml` is empty, so no source changed between that run and the batch base.
165: 
166: The first run of the subset on the repaired tree differed from that baseline in exactly one file, and it was a regression: `tests/InitOrderWithMutable.fss` compiled but its run exited 1 with
167: 
168:     NoSuchFieldError: Class InitOrderWithMutable$cvar does not have member field 'fortress.CompilerBuiltin$String ONLY'
169:       at InitOrderWithMutable$bvar.<clinit>
170: 
171: That program is `bvar = cvar` where `var cvar: String = avar` -- an immutable top-level variable whose initializer reads a *mutable* top-level variable declared later in the component. `forVarDeclPrePass` registered each variable's binding only as the loop reached it (`CodeGen.java:1858-1867` before the fix), so while `bvar`'s initializer was being generated `cvar` was not in the lexical environment and the read fell into `forVarRef`'s fresh-import path (`CodeGen.java:5952-5970`), which builds a plain `StaticBinding` and reads the singleton field with the *value's* descriptor. That is precisely the shape this repair changed.
172: 
173: The fix is in `forComponent` (`CodeGen.java:1857-1867`): every top-level variable's binding is registered for the whole component, by the new `addTopLevelVarBinding` (`CodeGen.java:5933-5951`), before any initializer is generated; `forVarDeclPrePass` (`:5908-5931`) now only generates the class. The alternative was to teach the fresh-import path to look the declaration's mutability up in the component index and build the matching binding there; I rejected it because it puts the mutability decision in two places, and because registering first also covers an object declaration's field initializer that refers to a variable declared after it, which the same mismatch would have hit. It costs nothing at run time and is the smaller statement of the same fact: the lexical environment is complete before any code that reads it is generated.
174: 
175: This is legitimate under the specification rather than a convenience: `Specification/basic/components/initialization.tex:12-16,29-30` has all top-level variables and singleton object fields initialized before their use, so an initializer that refers to a variable declared later in the component is a program the language admits -- and the tree has a test for exactly that, which is how this was caught.
176: 
177: The second run of the subset, after that fix, matches the baseline on all twenty files.
178: 
179: ## What this rung does not repair
180: 
181: A mutable *field* of an object is still outside the transaction (`VarCodeGen.MutableFieldVar:202-231`): decision 2 above, verified both ways by `probes/P10Field.fss` and under `walk`, and written out as a ledger row in `record.md`.
182: 
183: A top-level variable exported through an api still does not link, mutable or immutable (`probes/P8*`, `P9*`): pre-existing, unchanged by this rung, and written out as the second ledger row in `record.md`.
184: 
185: `atomic` used as an expression -- `atomic x := 1` rather than `atomic do x := 1 end` -- still has no visitor in `CodeGen` and reaches `defaultCase` (`map/spec-to-implementation.md:176`). Both new tests use the block form for that reason. `compiler_tests/Compiled170.fss`, which the inherited test comment cited as its model, is one of the programs that cannot compile for this reason and is in no `.test` file; the citation is gone.
186: 
187: Abrupt completion of an `atomic` block by anything other than a `TransactionAbortException` is not handled at all: `forAtomicBlock` catches only that class (`CodeGen.java:1737,1745`), so a Fortress exception thrown out of an `atomic` body leaves the task's transaction set and never committed or cleaned up. A deferred-write transaction discards the writes, which is what `atomic.tex:65-67` asks for, but the orphaned transaction stays current for the rest of the thread's work, and `atomic.tex:59-62`'s "writes within the block are retained" for an `exit` to an enclosing `label` is the opposite of what the same structure gives. I did not probe it and I am not claiming a defect here, only that the rung's repair does not reach it and that a reader who wants `atomic.tex:59-67` should start at `forAtomicBlock`.

205:     probes/pass-after-edit.txt       the recorded pass: the landed tree, same recipe

My skeptic refused this rung on one ground and it was right: the tree R1 landed turned a working program into a `java.lang.StackOverflowError`. A mutable variable whose declared type is a user-defined object or trait type, read or written inside `atomic do ... end`, printed the right answer on the batch base `49ee5e91` and crashed on the landed tree -- twelve lines, one thread, no concurrency (`probes/skeptic/SK25ObjNoAtomicVsAtomic.fss`; `SK18Trait` independently at trait type; both rows in `probes/skeptic/skeptic-basetree2.txt`, from one revert, rebuild, cache-wipe and library-order rebuild cycle).

The chain, which I re-read frame by frame rather than taking from the refusal. `Transaction.TXWrite` built its debug message by concatenation before testing the flag (`runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:227`; the flag is `private static boolean debug = false` at `:30` and `debug(String)` tests it only at `:56-58`, after Java has already built the argument). Concatenating the payload calls `MutableFValue.toString` (`runtimeValues/MutableFValue.java:38-40`), which renders the value, which for a compiled user object is `FValue.toString` (`runtimeValues/FValue.java:25-27`) -- `this.asString().toString()` -- and `trait Object`'s default `asString` is `jAsString(self)` (`LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:338`), bound to `stringOps.asString` (`:270`), which returns `a.toString()` (`nativeHelpers/stringOps.java:38-40`). fifth is the repair round.

> A mutable variable declared at the top level of a component is stored in a transactional cell on the compiled path: its singleton field is `ACC_FINAL` and holds a `MutableFValue`, reads and writes route through `Transaction.TXRead`/`TXWrite` while a transaction is running, and a nested code-generation context captures the cell rather than a copy of the value (`VarCodeGen.MutableStaticBinding`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/VarCodeGen.java:310-399`; `CodeGen.java:5872-5906`, `:4647-4650`, `:5908-5951`). Repaired 2026-09-19 by R1 of the repair batch; gated by `compiler_tests/MutableTopLevelVarInLoop` and `AtomicTopLevelObjectVar`, both deterministic and both failing at one thread on the tree each of them guards, and by `compiler_tests/AtomicTopLevelVar` under contention. **The bound**: this is `atomic` in a function body or a loop body. As the trailing expression of a `do … also` arm the generated class does not verify at all, before the repair or after (`VerifyError: Inconsistent stackmap frames`, ledger row 322), so "a top-level mutable variable is in the transaction" must not be read as "`atomic` on a top-level mutable variable works". > **The gate's thread count is inherited from the shell, and this repository pins it to one.** The chain is: the `fastTrack` macro that runs `compiler_tests` sets `FORTRESS_CACHES` and no thread count and no `newenvironment` (`build.xml:927-953`), so the forked JUnit JVM inherits the ambient environment; the harness runs each program in a further subprocess that inherits again (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:480-486`); and `FortressExecutable.getNumThreads` reads `FORTRESS_THREADS` first and only falls back to the processor count or `floor(n/2)` when it is unset (`:37-44`). `experiment/env.sh:6` exports `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`, every rung brief tells the agent to source it, and `explorations/coordinator/iteration-cost.md:126` records that no run in the climb used anything else — so in the gate as this project runs it, `compiler_tests` gets one worker. A concurrency defect on the compiled path is therefore **not** gateable by a concurrent test as the gate stands; it is gateable only by a test that fails at one thread. decisions: All fourteen debug call sites of Transaction.java are guarded, not only the nine that can crash. Failure recorded before the edit on the landed tree, pass recorded after a full rebuild and a library-order cache rebuild: 18 of 18 runs PASS across the four compiler_tests programs at one thread, unset and four. Two of the ruling's counts are corrected against the tree: twenty-three call sites, twenty-two eager. Eleven corrections applied to REPORT.md; five FACTS lines, three appends and six rows in record.md. Four commits pushed on wip/repair-r1-atomic-static; no forbidden file touched; the gate not run.
